fullName: Railway Recruitment Boards (RRB) Level-1 Examination, commonly called RRB Group D
overview: RRB Group D is the Railway Recruitment Boards' entry-level exam for **Level-1 posts of the 7th Pay Commission matrix** in Indian Railways: **Track Maintainer Grade-IV, Pointsman-B and a range of Assistant posts** (Track Machine, Bridge, P-Way, TRD, C&W, S&T, TL&AC and others). The academic bar is low, **Class 10 pass, or an ITI / NCVT-SCVT certificate, or NAC**, so each cycle attracts a crowd of lakhs of candidates for a pool of tens of thousands of seats. Selection is a four-step funnel: a single **100-question, 90-minute computer-based test**, then a **Physical Efficiency Test (PET)**, then **document verification** and a **medical examination**. The CBT score decides who is shortlisted and ranked; PET and medical are fitness hurdles you must clear. Prep therefore runs on two tracks: **sharpen General Science, Maths, Reasoning and Current Affairs** for the CBT, and **train for the load-carry and the 1000 m run** well before the PET call. Every post sits at **Pay Level 1 with an initial pay of ₹18,000 per month**.

latestCycle.notes:
The CBT is a single written stage, so there is no second written paper. The official answer-key notice confirms CBT from 3 to 25 August 2026. Vacancies are **RRB-wise and zone-wise**, you may submit **only one application**, and the RRB you choose cannot be changed afterwards. Shortlisting is **by normalised marks**. Result, PET and DV dates for CEN 09/2025 will be posted only on the official RRB websites (rrbcdg.gov.in links to all RRBs). Always confirm with the official notice.

stages.name: Computer Based Test (CBT)
stages.mode: Online CBT, objective multiple choice (four options)
stages.notes: Each question carries 1 mark. Duration is **90 minutes (120 minutes for PwBD candidates with a scribe)**. The paper is bilingual (English and Hindi) as per the CEN 08/2024 coverage; check the CEN 09/2025 notice for regional-language options. Mobile phones, calculators and electronic devices are banned in the exam hall. **Minimum qualifying percentage in the CBT:** UR and EWS 40%, OBC (non-creamy layer) 30%, SC 30%, ST 30%, with up to 2 marks of relaxation for PwBD if the panel cannot otherwise be filled. Scores are **normalised across shifts**.

stages.name: Physical Efficiency Test (PET)
stages.mode: Conducted by the RRCs / zonal railways
stages.notes: Candidates are shortlisted from the CBT at about **3 times the vacancies** (railway/RRC-wise and community-wise; the ratio can change with the administration's requirement). **Men:** carry 35 kg over 100 m in 2 minutes without putting it down, then run 1000 m in 4 minutes 15 seconds. **Women:** carry 20 kg over 100 m in 2 minutes, then run 1000 m in 5 minutes 40 seconds. Exempt from PET: PwBD candidates, Course Completed Act Apprentices and ex-servicemen; pregnant candidates can ask for the test to be deferred on a temporary-unfitness declaration.

stages.name: Document Verification (DV) and Medical Examination
stages.mode: Conducted by the RRBs / railway administration
stages.notes: After PET, candidates are called for DV in merit order at about **1 time the vacancies**, then undergo the medical examination (fitness per the medical category of the post, listed in the notice's annexure). Selection by the RRB does not by itself guarantee appointment; the final offer comes from the railway administration.

eligibility.nationality: Citizen of India. Citizens of Nepal and Bhutan, Tibetan refugees who came before 1 January 1962, and persons of Indian origin from specified countries (with a government eligibility certificate) are also allowed under the usual railway rules.

selectionProcess: **CBT → PET → Document Verification (DV) → Medical Examination (ME).** About **3 times the vacancies** are shortlisted from the CBT for PET (railway/RRC-wise and community-wise), and about **1 time the vacancies** are called for DV, in merit order. To be considered you need the **minimum CBT percentage: 40% for UR and EWS, 30% for OBC-NCL, SC and ST**, with up to 2 marks of relaxation for PwBD where needed. PET and the medical are qualifying; CBT marks (normalised) drive the merit order. You apply to **one RRB only**, and the notice states that multiple applications lead to rejection of all of them and debarment. There is **no interview**. Note that the 11-post vacancy list shown here adds up to fewer than the 22,195 total, so the notice may list further posts not captured here.
normalization: Because the CBT runs over many days and shifts with different papers, RRBs **normalise marks** across sessions and use the normalised marks for shortlisting at every stage. The practical lessons: (1) don't compare raw scores with friends in other shifts; (2) the scorecard shows both raw and normalised marks; (3) a tougher shift is compensated, so don't panic and attempt only what you can answer with reasonable confidence, since each wrong answer costs 1/3 mark. The exact formula is in the RRB notice and is not reproduced here.

faqs.q: What is the RRB Group D exam pattern?
faqs.a: One online test of **100 questions, 100 marks, 90 minutes**: General Science (25), Mathematics (25), General Intelligence & Reasoning (30) and General Awareness & Current Affairs (20). Each question carries **1 mark** and each wrong answer costs **1/3 mark**.

faqs.q: What is the age limit for RRB Group D?
faqs.a: For CEN 09/2025 it is **18–33 years as on 1 January 2026**. Relaxations include +3 years for OBC-NCL, +5 for SC/ST, and more for ex-servicemen, PwBD and widowed/divorced women (upper limit 35/38/40). Relaxations are not cumulative.
A **Class 10 pass, an ITI (NCVT/SCVT) certificate or a National Apprenticeship Certificate**. An engineering diploma cannot replace ITI.

faqs.q: Which posts does Group D cover and what is the pay?
faqs.a: Track Maintainer Grade-IV, Pointsman-B and Assistant posts such as Track Machine, Bridge, P-Way, TRD, C&W, S&T, TL&AC and Loco Shed (Electrical). All are **Pay Level 1 with an initial pay of ₹18,000** per month, plus allowances that vary by posting.

faqs.q: How many vacancies are there in the latest cycle?
faqs.a: **22,195** under CEN 09/2025, notified on 30 January 2026. The earlier cycle, CEN 08/2024, had **32,438** vacancies. Track Maintainer Grade-IV is the largest post (9,350 in CEN 09/2025), followed by Pointsman-B (4,843).

**Men:** carry 35 kg for 100 m in 2 minutes, then run 1000 m in 4 min 15 s. **Women:** carry 20 kg for 100 m in 2 minutes, then run 1000 m in 5 min 40 s. It is qualifying only. PwBD candidates, ex-servicemen and Course Completed Act Apprentices are exempt.

faqs.q: What is the minimum qualifying percentage in the CBT?
faqs.a: **40% for UR and EWS; 30% for OBC-NCL, SC and ST**, with up to 2 marks of relaxation for PwBD where the panel cannot be filled. Clearing the minimum is not enough: only about 3 times the vacancies are called for PET, so the actual cut-off is higher.
**₹500** for General/OBC/EWS (₹400 refunded after you appear in the CBT) and **₹250** for SC/ST, ex-servicemen, PwBD, women, transgender, minorities and EBC (refunded after you appear).

faqs.q: Is there a Tier 2 or an interview?
faqs.a: No. The written stage is a single CBT, followed by PET, document verification and the medical examination. There is no interview.

faqs.q: Is the CEN 09/2025 result out yet?
faqs.a: In the sources checked up to 1 October 2026, **no official result date had been announced**. The CBT answer key was released on 7 September 2026. Treat any specific date on unofficial sites as a guess and check your RRB's website.

faqs.q: Can I apply to more than one RRB?
faqs.a: No. Only one application is allowed; submitting more than one can lead to rejection of all of them and debarment. The RRB and zone you pick cannot be changed after registration.

faqs.q: Do PET marks count in the merit?
faqs.a: No. PET and the medical examination are qualifying; they decide whether you stay in the process, while your normalised CBT score decides your place in merit.

documents: At document verification, keep originals ready of: **Class 10 certificate** or ITI/NAC certificate (with issue dates; proof of age and qualification), a **valid photo ID** (Aadhaar, voter ID, driving licence or similar), **community certificate** (SC/ST/OBC-NCL/EWS) in the prescribed format if you claimed it, **disability certificate** if you claimed PwBD benefits, **ex-servicemen documents** if applicable, a recent **passport-size photograph** (not older than 2 months), your **admit card/scorecard**, and any further documents the call letter lists. Mismatches in name or date of birth between documents can cancel your candidature, so fix them early.

calendar.note: The official CEN 09/2025 answer-key notice confirms CBT on 3–25 August and the response/objection window on 7–17 September. Later result and PET announcements must be checked separately on the unified RRB portal.
